decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach toward the lone orange ring; rotate gradually to a downward grasp while staying in the right workspace.
Advance above the orange ring and finish vertical alignment; stop above grasp depth to check the wrist view.
Use the wrist image to center the orange ring, lower to grasp height, then close fully. Retention remains to be checked after lifting.
Lift the closed orange grasp clear of the table and transport toward the shortest, rightmost peg. Check RGB retention and peg alignment next.
Center the retained orange ring above the rightmost short peg and approach slowly, leaving clearance for wrist-camera alignment.
Lower orange gently toward its short peg while beginning an elbow-up left-arm approach for the yellow pieces. Keep orange closed until insertion is visually checked.
Seat and release the orange ring over the visible short peg, then retreat vertically. Center the left gripper over the nearer yellow square for inspection.
Align and close on the nearer yellow square. Move the open right gripper aside to inspect whether the orange ring actually seated; its last view was ambiguous.
Lift and carry the closed yellow grasp toward the left pegs. Reapproach the orange ring using its visible offset from the short peg; it does not yet look fully inserted.
Hover the retained yellow piece over the tall left peg. Regrasp and lift orange to expose its peg and resolve the apparent insertion offset visually.
Correct yellow toward the visible peg before descending. The orange regrasp was empty, so reopen and approach lower to engage its edges.
Account for wrist-camera parallax: lower yellow toward its peg while restoring its board-plane alignment. Recenter the orange grasp closer to the robot before closing.
The tall peg is visible through yellow's hole; seat and release it. Lift orange clear, correct its offset toward the exposed short peg, then approach again.
Seat and release orange with its peg now visible through the hole. Move the open left arm to the remaining left-side yellow square.
Retry the rejected, unexecuted approach with the erroneous rotation entry corrected: grasp left yellow and hover above the near right yellow.
Lift the second yellow and carry it above the tall left peg. Align and grasp the nearer right yellow, retaining zero opening while carrying.
Lower the second yellow onto the tall peg for alignment inspection. Carry the right yellow to a central staging area for a sequential, non-crossing transfer.
Back the tilted yellow away from peg contact to inspect retention. Replan the interrupted right-arm transfer with smaller increments and reduced height.
The left square slipped into an edge grip; set it aside for a flat regrasp rather than forcing insertion. Deposit the right yellow at the center boundary for sequential transfer.
Withdraw the right arm to the last right-side yellow. Approach the centrally staged yellow with the left arm without crossing; leave the edge-standing square for later recovery.
Replan with small increments after the guard. Align gripper jaws with each square and descend to centered grasps on the staged yellow and the last right-side yellow.
Lift both centered yellow grasps; bring the left square above its peg and begin the right square's transfer toward the center, maintaining arm separation.
Slowly insert the centered left yellow and inspect before release. Bring the right yellow to the center staging location with reduced height to maintain reach margin.
Relieve the yellow rim contact, make a small lateral correction, and release above the peg rather than forcing the tilted piece. Deposit the last right yellow at the center and withdraw.
The released yellow fell off the peg; approach the now-flat left square for a centered retry. Clear the right arm toward the right-side purple piece without crossing.
Make small wrist-image centering corrections, lower to the piece edges, and close on the flat left yellow and right purple.
Lift before transport. Bring yellow above the tall peg using the updated visual estimate; carry purple toward a separate front-center staging area for a non-crossing transfer.
Approach the yellow peg only to its tip, then pause for a settled wrist view. Move purple to the front-center staging point, preserving separate arm workspaces.
Relieve contact and adjust yellow a few millimeters toward the visible peg tip before slow insertion. Release purple at the boundary staging point and withdraw the right arm.
Back yellow out of rim contact and correct toward the peg visible at the near side of its hole; pause to inspect. Approach the remaining center-right purple with the open right arm.
Use the now-exposed peg position to realign yellow horizontally while clear of contact. Center and grasp the purple piece with the right arm.
The peg tip is now visible within yellow's hole. Lower gently, release over that alignment, and withdraw. Lift purple and move toward a separate front staging area.
Withdraw from the released yellow to let it settle. Approach the accessible left purple piece while clearing the empty right gripper away from the center.
Move the left grasp away from the overlapping yellow edge, center on purple and lift to verify retention. Reapproach the center-right purple independently.
The left purple grasp was empty; move clear and approach the isolated blue piece instead. Reorient and lower the right gripper for a centered purple grasp.
Grasp the isolated blue rectangle. Lift the right purple grasp to verify retention and carry it toward the front-center transfer area.
Deposit the retained purple in a clear front-center spot and withdraw right. Lift blue and carry it toward a separate forward staging spot for the opposite-arm transfer.
Place blue at a clear forward boundary location for a sequential handoff. Move the right arm away before bringing the left arm toward the center.
Shift the blue staging point away from the robot's front hardware, lower onto the table, and release before the right arm approaches.
Withdraw the left arm fully before the right arm approaches the staged blue. Keep both EE centers on their own side of the centerline.
Approach the unobstructed left purple. Align the right jaws with the staged blue's rotation, lower around its edges, and close without crossing the centerline.
Lift both grasps and keep the left purple safely aside. Carry blue over its third peg for a separate, closely observed insertion.
The left purple was not retained; approach the remaining blue instead. Align the retained right blue toward the visible peg tip before a shallow descent.
Make a millimeter-scale correction to the blue hole over the visible peg, then descend slowly without releasing. Grasp the remaining blue with the left arm.
Blue's peg is visibly through the hole; seat it a little farther, release, and withdraw. Lift the remaining blue and carry it toward the front transfer area.
Replan from the interrupted observation: separate the arms and clear the peg area first, then carry the retained blue along a front route rather than beside the other gripper.
Lower and release the retained blue at the forward boundary staging point, with the right arm safely withdrawn. Prepare right-gripper orientation for the next pickup.
Clear the left gripper from the staged blue before the right approaches. Bring the left arm above the now-isolated purple for a corrected, centered pickup.
Use settled wrist views for small centering corrections and lower both grippers to centered grasps: left purple and staged right blue.
Lift both pieces to verify retention. Keep the left purple well away while bringing the second blue above the third peg for a careful alignment check.
Hold purple safely clear. Correct the blue hole toward the exposed peg region and make only a shallow descent, reserving release until the alignment is visible.
Lower blue slowly along the apparent peg axis, keeping the grip closed and the other arm clear; inspect for seating or rim contact before release.
The peg is visible through blue's hole. Apply a small centering correction and descend gently toward the stack, keeping the left arm stationary and clear.
Relieve the blue stack's contact rather than pushing farther. Recenter toward the peg axis and release at a higher seating height so the pieces can settle freely.
Withdraw the right gripper completely to let blue settle. Only after clearance, bring the retained purple above its second peg for a fresh visual alignment.
Align the purple hole to the exposed second peg tip using the wrist displacement, then make a shallow descent. Keep the right arm parked and clear.
Make a small correction toward the peg seen at the upper edge of purple's hole, then lower one millimeter per step and inspect before release.
The exposed second peg is now visible below-left of purple. Correct toward that actual tip, then descend cautiously while holding; the earlier bright hole edge was ambiguous.
The purple left the grip near its peg; open and withdraw vertically to let it settle, then approach the forward purple with a corrected downward orientation.
Center on the nearer forward purple using the settled wrist image, descend vertically to the piece edges, and close while keeping the right arm parked.
Lift the newly closed purple grasp clear, then hover above its second peg with an allowance for the hole's offset within the fingers. Keep right parked.
